note: The heart-failure benefit was found in patients first (EMPA-REG OUTCOME, 2015) and the HFrEF outcome trials were already enrolling before the first heart-failure animal model was published, so every model here was built to explain a clinical result, not to predict one.
label: Heart failure (SGLT2)

engagement.note: Empagliflozin lowered cardiomyocyte Na+ via NHE1 inhibition; this cardiac target was proposed after EMPA-REG and never measured in patients.
engagement.short: Cardiac NHE1 target proposed post hoc
engagement.quote: The glucose lowering kidney-targeted agent, EMPA, demonstrates direct cardiac effects by lowering myocardial [Na+]c and [Ca2+]c and enhancing [Ca2+]m, through impairment of myocardial NHE flux, independent of SGLT2 activity.
engagement.reason: No patient measurement of any proposed target
engagement.judgement: The renal target (SGLT2 inhibition, glucosuria) was validated in the type 2 diabetes programme, not in this context, and the HFrEF trials measured no engagement read-out. The only HF-specific target proposal, cardiac NHE1, was made in rat/rabbit cardiomyocytes (online Oct 2016) after EMPA-REG and later failed to replicate in rat cardiomyocytes and perfused mouse/rat/guinea-pig hearts (Chung 2021, https://doi.org/10.1093/cvr/cvaa323: 'cardiac NHE1 activity is not inhibited by EMPA'). That is model-vs-model, not model-vs-patient, so the status stays untested rather than contra. Abstract-level reading; the quote's sub/superscripts ([Na+]c, [Ca2+]c, [Ca2+]m) were reconstructed from a PubMed abstract that stripped them.

dose.note: Mice got 10 mg/kg/day; the HF trials reused the 10 mg diabetes dose, and no HF model set or tested an exposure target.
dose.short: Diabetes dose reused; no HF exposure target
dose.quote: Mice considered to be in heart failure (%EF <45%) were randomly assigned to receive either vehicle (0.5% hydroxyethyl cellulose [Natrosol]) (Sigma-Aldrich, Ontario, Canada) or empagliflozin (MedChemExpress, Princeton, New Jersey) (10 mg/kg/day) for 2 weeks by oral gavage.
dose.reason: Dose came from diabetes, not a model
dose.judgement: DAPA-HF (https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1911303, 'dapagliflozin (at a dose of 10 mg once daily)') and EMPEROR-Reduced (https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2022190) each tested the single approved type 2 diabetes dose; there was no HF dose-ranging and no model-derived exposure or occupancy target. The pig MI model (Santos-Gallego 2019) likewise used one fixed dose. The FDA review for the HFrEF supplement (NDA 202293 S-020, https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/202293Orig1s020.pdf) could not be downloaded (bot block), so its dose-rationale and nonclinical sections are unverified. Full text of Byrne 2017 read via PMC.

efficacy.model: Non-diabetic TAC mouse with reduced EF
efficacy.note: First HF model for the class, built after EMPA-REG (2015) while DAPA-HF and EMPEROR-Reduced were already enrolling; no model-to-patient comparison published.
efficacy.short: Models came after the patient signal
efficacy.quote: Together, our data show for the first time that empagliflozin treatment of nondiabetic mice with reduced EF heart failure blunts the progressive decline in cardiac function both in vivo and ex vivo.
efficacy.judgement: Chronology: EMPA-REG OUTCOME (https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1504720, Sept 2015) found the 35% HF-hospitalization reduction in a cardiovascular-safety trial of a glucose-lowering drug. A PubMed sweep for SGLT2-inhibitor/phlorizin cardiac animal studies 2008 to Sept 2015 found only diabetic-mouse fibrosis/oxidative-stress work (Lin 2014, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12933-014-0148-1) and a negative-inotropy finding in STZ-rat myocytes (Hamouda 2014, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11010-014-2262-5): nothing that predicted a heart-failure benefit. Byrne 2017, the first non-diabetic HFrEF model, says so itself: 'despite ongoing clinical trials in HF patients without type 2 diabetes, there are no objective and translational data to support an effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on cardiac structure and function'. The closest thing to a prospective model-to-patient test: the non-diabetic pig MI model (Santos-Gallego 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2019.01.056) generated the same group's EMPA-TROPISM hypothesis (design paper, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10557-018-06850-0: 'we hypothesized that the cardiac benefits of empagliflozin can also be extended to non-diabetic HF patients'), and EMPA-TROPISM (n=84, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2020.11.008) found reverse remodeling (LVEDV -25.1 vs -1.5 ml) in non-diabetic HFrEF. I did not award `same` because (a) the pig model was built to explain EMPA-REG and post-dates the decision to run the outcome trials, (b) the result paper's abstract makes no comparison with the animal data and the full text is paywalled (JACC returned 403), (c) the endpoint is an imaging surrogate and DAPA-HF had already shown outcome benefit in non-diabetic patients. Flip to `same` (2021, model 'Non-diabetic pig MI') only if the atlas counts a post-hoc model's prospective surrogate-endpoint test.
